links.outcome: Discrimination of incorrect LLM responses (AUROC) to MRCOG obstetrics and gynaecology questions
links.effect: Full dataset (n=1670): AUROC 0·76 [95% CI 0·75-0·78] for semantic entropy vs 0·62 [0·60-0·65] for perplexity. Expert-validated subset (105 questions): 0·97 [0·91-1·00] vs 0·57 [0·405-0·68]. Discrete semantic entropy, which needs no model internals, performed similarly.
links.tradeoff: Semantic clustering, required for semantic entropy, succeeded in only 30% of questions, though it still gave informative uncertainty signals when incomplete. Each item was entered into the LLM ten times to compute the score.
links.quote: Semantic entropy showed superior discrimination of incorrect responses compared with perplexity (AUROC 0·76 [95% CI 0·75-0·78 vs 0·62 [0·60-0·65]).

design_hint: uncertainty-based flagging of LLM outputs (semantic entropy)
